children: Speakers at the ‘Mangaluru Technovanza 2026’, organised by the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM), have stressed the need to focus on specialised competencies and capabilities to build technology ecosystem in coastal Karnataka  region.

Speaking at a panel discussion on ‘Policy, Industry, Capital’ as part of the ‘Mangaluru Technovanza’, Devdutt Yellurkar, General Partner, Charles River Ventures, said Mangaluru region has to figure out its core competency to scale on.

Highlighting Mangaluru’s strength in healthcare sector, he quoted his own example. Stating that he has a special heart condition, Yellurkar said his cardiologist Maneesh Rai had put him into contact with research universities in the region that are doing cutting edge research on DNA analysis.

“They have really commendable stuff that compares to anything that happens in Stanford. Can we leverage some of that with technology and build clusters around it, and truly become world class. If we build that, venture capital funds will come,” he said.

Referring to the Karnataka government’s decision to upgrade Fisheries College in Mangaluru into a marine university, he asked the technology ecosystem to focus on exploring opportunities in ocean science.
Referring to his association with Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution in the US, he said if anybody wants to know anything about ocean science, they visit Woods Hole.

He and others have built a cluster around the ideas that are coming out in the field of ocean science. “We are investing in research that is coming out of different universities working on ocean science,” he said, adding, the cluster was built around nearly 100-year-old Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution.
He said he is ready to make introduction on ocean science in the US to the technology ecosystem from coastal Karnataka, if it is interested in connecting with the research universities in the US.
He urged the technology ecosystem in coastal Karnataka to focus on the quality. That will solve the problem of capital, he said.

Prashanth Shenoy, Co-Founder and CTO of UniCourt, Mangaluru, who moderated the session, said the government’s focus on ocean science and Yellurkar’s expertise could help do something related to ocean science in coastal Karnataka.
BV Naidu, Chairman of KDEM, and LK Atheeq, Financial Advisor to the Karnataka Chief Minister, also spoke on the occasion.

Meanwhile, a fireside conversation on GCCs with Ajay Vij, Senior Country MD, Accenture India, and Richard Lobo, Chief People Officer of Tech Mahindra, explored Mangaluru’s potential as an emerging technology destination.

Vij said it is necessary to decide the niche Mangaluru needs to play up. Cities like this need to build specialised capabilities, and not just replicate the existing ecosystems. He said local innovation can create global impact by solving challenges that matter.
Lobo said GCCs were focusing on cost and proprietary model earlier. However, now they are shifting from cost advantage to capability and innovation-led models, he said.
Sanjeev Kumar Gupta, CEO of KDEM, moderated the fireside chat.

title: Tech ecosystem in coastal Karnataka asked to focus on competencies, capabilities
